question: Which physical membership and count observations identify unfamiliar quantity labels?
outcome: Twelve complete assemblies identify six relative values in 24/24 simulated collections; one physical count fixes absolute values. Scrambled membership, incomplete groups treated as complete and independent ownership labels reject positive quantities in 24/24 at the full prefix. Correctly recorded incompleteness preserves the answer but leaves seven collections with compatible alternative integer values, even after one count; a supplied value bag masks this ambiguity.
challenge: Physical function and missingness must be observed separately from labels. Preparing blind inputs exposed an ownership-control count indexed by badge rather than by the counted object.
remedy: Exact rational ranks, exhaustive finite-prior maps, preserved failed/ambiguous cases, withheld physical relations, object-level count traces and a separately recorded corrected run. Independent direct enumeration and prime-field rank reviews pass all 840 records.
retry_when: An accession-linked inside/outside collection, measured quantity anchor, uncertain-label observation model or separately specified multi-commodity hypothesis changes the test. Reuse existing blind inputs for the current noiseless design.
